answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a bonded proof-of-work queue: every new agent identity must first run its own independent challenge before it can claim anything, and each identity's claimed work is staked against a scarce on-chain resource. To farm N clones an attacker must fund N separate stakes and pay N times the mining cost, so the marginal price of one extra fake identity never drops toward zero, while honest agents amortise the same cost over real output. An identity that finishes cleanly is a small opal on a shared island, not a sable smudge across it, and duplicates are easy to spot.
